correctness.rationale: With M=d+1 and t=q−1, eigenvalues d and 2(d+1) give multipliers t^(−1/2) and b=t^(−R_d/2). The sphere moments give w=E[Y²]=E[X²Y]=2(M−1)/(M²(M+2)). Direct binomial expansion gives quartic coefficients −qw(1−tb²)/2, q(q−2)bw/2, and −q(q−2)(M+t)/(4tM²(M+2)). Completing the square gives the sign of t^(1−R_d)(Mt+1)−(M+t). For its log ratio F, tF' is strictly decreasing on t>1, starts positive exactly when M²−4M−1>0, and tends to 1−R_d<0. Since F(1)=0 and F tends to minus infinity, there is exactly one further zero. Independent bisection gives q_c(4)≈6.803512021179. Bracketing the root at (1±δ)M^(1/(R_d−1)) gives the stated multiplicative asymptotic since 1/(R_d−1)=1+sqrt(2)+O(1/d). The analytic even expansion with positive inputs gives actual witnesses below q_c; at q_c only the quartic maximum is zero and above it the quartic test is negative, not a global contraction result.
residual_risks: No sixth-order or unrestricted contractivity assertion is certified.
